info.title: Streamer Toolkit Host
info.description: Local Host API on 127.0.0.1. `/ws/overlay` is a read-only WebSocket: the first message is a `Snapshot`, then events such as `ChatMessageEvent`, `AlertEvent`, `ObsStatusEvent`, `TemplateChangedEvent`, `RedemptionChangedEvent`, `CheckinChangedEvent`, `CheckinStampedEvent`, `SoundPlayEvent` and `SoundStoppedEvent` follow in `seq` order.

get.summary: The saved choice; `null` when never changed (numbers show).

put.summary: Saves the choice; at most 50 revealed IDs of 1-32 characters `[a-z0-9.-]`.

get.summary: The latest alerts this launch, newest first (at most 50), with what became of each.

post.summary: Queues an alert from 最近事件 again with the current template and sounds; nothing is recorded again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The alert's ID from 最近事件

get.summary:
A `.stbackup` file of this data folder: its data (settings and the database), its media (custom templates, sounds,
music, videos and GIFs, card images) or both. Live use goes on while it is made; database writes wait only for the
snapshot.

parameters.name: contents
parameters.description: Only this kind; both when absent.

413.description: `backup.too_large`: more than a restore accepts (20 GB unpacked, 100,000 files)

507.description: `backup.no_space`, with `needed` (bytes): not enough free disk space

post.summary:
Restores the staged backup: the app restarts, backs up the current data of the kinds it holds to `backups/`,
then puts the backup in place before the database opens.

Starts a restore upload of a file of `size` bytes, replacing any earlier upload. Refused before anything is written
when the file is above the cap or the disk has less than twice its size free (the upload, then its unpacked copy).

put.summary: Adds the next part (the body, at most 16 MB) at `offset`, which must be the bytes received so far.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: From the upload's start

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Where this part starts: the bytes received so far.

400.description: `backup.invalid`: past the size given at the start

409.description: `backup.upload_offset`, with `received`: not where the upload stands

500.description: `backup.restore_failed`: could not be written; the upload is dropped

delete.summary: Cancels the upload and removes what arrived; one already gone is fine.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: From the upload's start

post.summary:
Checks the complete upload and stages it for a restore (as the one-request preview did); nothing in use changes.
The uploaded file is removed either way.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: From the upload's start

400.description: `backup.invalid`: damaged or not a backup; `backup.newer_version`: made by a newer version

409.description: `backup.upload_offset`, with `received`: not all of it has arrived

get.summary: How large the data and the media are now, for choosing what to back up.
The chat display settings; `null` when never changed (the admin UI shows its defaults).

put.summary: Saves the chat display settings; `textSize` is 80-150 in steps of 10.

get.summary: The panel's state; `null` when never changed (the admin UI shows its defaults).

put.summary: Saves the panel's state; `width` is 280-560.

get.summary:
Twitch's global chat badges and the broadcaster's own (subscriber badges and the like), read once per launch;
empty while signed out or when Twitch cannot be reached, so chat just shows no badge images.
The chat bots the leaderboard leaves out and the chat log can hide (lowercase logins).
The stored messages, follows, subs, cheers, raids and redemptions from `from` until `to`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: RFC 3339; open when left out.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: RFC 3339, not included; open when left out.

get.summary: The latest 200 stored chat messages from Twitch, oldest first.

The latest streams, newest first, with the chat between them; stretches between streams with no chat are left
out.

400.description: `chat.send_invalid` (empty or over 500 characters), `chat.send_refused` (Twitch refused the message), or not signed in

422.description: `chat.send_dropped`: Twitch took the message but did not send it (e.g. a duplicate or AutoMod)

put.summary: Saves the style; the next card on the overlay shows it.

400.description: `checkin.invalid_style`: out of range, or an image the folder does not have

post.summary:
在 OBS 試播: shows a sample card in the saved style through the presentation queue (`source=simulation`);
nothing is recorded.
隱藏畫面卡片: takes the stamp card on the screen away at once.

get.summary: The change log: the latest 100 deductions, newest first.

post.summary: Copies a PNG, JPG, GIF or WebP image (at most 5 MB, no SVG) in for the style. The body is the file itself.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The original file name: its extension must match the content.

400.description: `checkin.unsupported_image`: not a PNG, JPG, GIF or WebP file (by extension and content)

post.summary: Imports the file in one transaction; the same file imported again gives the same totals.

requestBody.description: The import file: an object keyed by Twitch user ID (at most 5 MB)

400.description: `checkin.import_invalid`: not JSON, or not an object

post.summary: What importing this file would change; nothing is written. The admin UI posts the chosen file's content.

requestBody.description: The import file: an object keyed by Twitch user ID (at most 5 MB)

400.description: `checkin.import_invalid`: not JSON, or not an object

post.summary: Puts a dead letter back in line with a fresh set of attempts.
Gives up on a dead letter: that redemption never checks in.

Installs an animation pack: a zip (at most 10 MB) with `pack.json` (`{"name": …}`), `index.html` and CSS,
images, fonts or sounds. The body is the zip itself.

400.description: `card_pack.invalid` or `card_pack.script`, with the file (and place) in `detail`

delete.summary: Removes a pack; a card style that used it falls back to the simple style.

get.summary:
Helix Get Custom Reward (scope `channel:read:redemptions`). A channel without channel points is refused by
Twitch: 502 `twitch.request_refused`.

409.description: `commands.taken`: another feature's command has the name

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the login or display name; ASCII letters ignore case.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Viewers to skip; default 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100; default 50.

post.summary: Puts the viewer's stamp card on the screen through the presentation queue; no check-in is recorded.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The viewer's internal ID

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The viewer's ID

200.description: Recorded, or already checked in that day

400.description: `checkin.invalid_date`: not a date, or a future business day

post.summary: Spends a viewer's stamps; the total and the card stay as they are.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The viewer's internal ID

400.description: `checkin.invalid_deduction`: an amount out of range or a reason too long

post.summary: Adds a counter at 0. A per-stream one counts the stream on now as already reset.

400.description: `counter.invalid`: an empty name, a command that is not one word, or more than 100 counters

get.summary: The sub marathon timer now (also kept current by `counter.marathon`).

post.summary: Adds or takes minutes by hand.
Pauses or resumes by hand; a stream starting never resumes it.

get.summary: The per-viewer counters with their totals and top three.

400.description: `counter.invalid`: an empty name, or more than 100 per-viewer counters

delete.summary: Deletes a per-viewer counter and every viewer's count in it.

post.summary: Adds or takes one for a viewer.

404.description: `counter.not_found`, or `counter.viewer_not_found`: not in the viewer directory

get.summary: Every viewer above 0, most first.

Viewers in the viewer directory whose login or display name contains `q` (at most 20, most recently seen
first), with their count in this counter.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a login or display name.

put.summary: Changes a counter's settings; its value stays. Becoming per-stream counts the stream on now as already reset.

delete.summary: Deletes a counter and its chat command.

post.summary: Adds or takes one.
Puts a counter back to 0.

get.summary: Checks the connections now (one Helix call when signed in).
The latest 200 log lines at or above a level, newest first.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The least severe level to list: `error`, `warn` or `info` (default `info`).

get.summary:
A report to share when asking for help: versions, connections, modules turned off and the latest warnings and
errors as time, level and code only.

This stream's (or since launch, before the first stream) latest 50 alerts, redemptions and check-ins, newest
first.
A stage's tile IDs in display order; `null` when never arranged (the admin UI shows that stage's defaults).

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: `before`, `live` (the default) or `after`.

put.summary:
Saves a stage's tile order: up to 50 IDs of 1-32 characters `[a-z0-9-]`; duplicates keep their first position.
`null` restores that stage's defaults; `[]` keeps it empty. The other stages are left as they are.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: `before`, `live` (the default) or `after`.

post.summary:
Resizes a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP picture (at most 10 MB and 4096 px a side; the body is the file itself) to the
sizes of `kind`, as JSON with previews or, with `zip=true`, as one zip of PNG files.

parameters.name: zip
parameters.description: `zip`: every size in one zip file; otherwise JSON with a preview of each.

parameters.name: crop_x
parameters.description:
With `fit=manual`: the rectangle's left edge, top edge, width and height in the picture's pixels; it must lie
inside the picture.

parameters.name: bg
parameters.description: The padding's color as six hex digits (`1f2937`); transparent when missing.

400.description: `image_sizes.unsupported`, or `image_sizes.invalid_crop`: a manual rectangle missing or outside the picture, or `image_sizes.invalid_bg`: a padding color that is not six hex digits

413.description: `image_sizes.too_large`: more than 10 MB or 4096 px a side

get.summary: The input chosen as the mic; `null` when none is.

put.summary:
Chooses the mic (an input name of 1-256 characters without control characters), or clears it with `null`. The
input is not checked against OBS, which may be closed; the mixer says so when it is missing.

post.summary: Copies an MP3, WAV or OGG file (at most 50 MB) into the music library. The body is the file itself.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The original file name: its extension must match the content; the rest becomes the title.

400.description: `music.unsupported_type`: not an MP3, WAV or OGG file (by extension and content)

post.summary: Plays, pauses, skips, stops or seeks; the result arrives as a `bgm.player` event.

409.description: `music.nothing_to_play`: none of its tracks can play (files gone, lengths not measured); `music.off`: the feature is turned off

put.summary: Sets the music volume and whether playlists play shuffled.

post.summary:
Plays the first playable track of the playlist chosen last on the music overlay for 5 seconds, as a `bgm.test`
event (`source=simulation`, not kept in snapshots). The player, its track and its position do not change.

409.description: `music.nothing_to_play`: no playlist chosen yet, or none of its tracks can play; `music.playing`: the music is playing; `music.off`: the feature is turned off

post.summary: Adds an empty playlist at the end.

put.summary: Renames a playlist.

delete.summary: Deletes a playlist; its tracks stay in the library. The scene rules that played it lose it and are disabled.

put.summary:
Replaces every scene rule, in order: the first enabled rule naming a scene plays on it. Saving does not apply
them to the scene on air; the next scene switch does.

400.description: `music.invalid`: an empty name, a volume over 100, a scene name over 256 characters, an enabled rule without a playlist, or more than 100 rules

put.summary: Renames a track.

delete.summary: Deletes a track, takes it out of every playlist, and deletes its file.

put.summary:
Records how long a track plays; the admin window measures each track after import, and unmeasured ones when
the music page opens.
Chooses which playlists a track is in.
Saves the address (and the password, when given) and reconnects with them.

Changes an input's fader, mute or monitoring (they belong to the input, in every scene); `obs.state` shows the
change once OBS has made it.
Shows, hides, locks, unlocks or moves a scene item; `obs.state` shows the change once OBS has made it.

get.summary:
The inputs' latest audio levels (OBS's volume meters), for the mixer to poll while it shows; empty while OBS is
not connected.
The canvas size and where each item of a scene sits (asked when the scene page shows the scene).

put.summary: Puts a scene in the preview while studio mode is on; `obs.state`'s `preview` shows it.
Puts a scene on air; `obs.state` shows the switch once OBS has made it.

get.summary: The listed settings of one source, for its form.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: The source's name (a scene item's `source` in `obs.state`).

put.summary:
Changes listed settings of one source; refused for a kind without a form, a field not on its form, a value of
the wrong shape, or an address that is not one of this Host's overlays.

get.summary: The choices OBS offers for one listed field of a capture or audio source.

parameters.name: property
parameters.description: One of the form's listed fields: `video_device_id`, `resolution`, `window`, `capture_mode`.

post.summary: Reloads a browser source's page (OBS's 「重新整理快取」); other kinds are refused.

get.summary: Where this Host's overlays are in OBS: one entry per browser source showing one, with the scenes it is in.

post.summary:
Puts an overlay in a scene: the browser source already showing it gets a new item there, or a new browser
source opens the overlay's address on this Host (never with a token). Only while OBS runs on this computer.

delete.summary:
Takes an overlay out of a scene: removes that scene's items whose source shows the overlay. Items of other
sources are never touched; the sources stay in the other scenes.

parameters.name: overlay
parameters.description: The overlay's path and query, as in `GET /api/admin/obs/sources`.

put.summary: Turns OBS's studio mode on or off; `obs.state` follows once OBS has done it, also when it is changed in OBS.

get.summary: How an item is turned, flipped, cropped and fitted (asked when its 變形 tab opens).

get.summary: How many OBS sources each overlay has open right now.
The latest sample; `null` until the first one (2 seconds after start).

What is on, with the new poll

`polls.invalid`: one is over Twitch's limits, or more than 20

post.summary: Cancels every waiting item; the one playing finishes. Records (redemptions, check-ins) are not touched.

Records (redemptions, check-ins) are not touched.

Emergency stop: ends the item playing and cancels the waiting ones; overlays stop picture and sound at once.
Records (redemptions, check-ins) are not touched.

get.summary: How many records keeping only `days` days would delete now; asked before shortening the retention.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The retention to check, 1-3650 days.

get.summary: How long chat and activity records are kept: `{"days": n}` or `"forever"`.

put.summary:
Saves the retention (1-3650 days, or forever) and deletes the records it no longer keeps, together: a failed
save deletes nothing. The admin UI asks before shortening it and reads the retention again after an error.

500.description: `settings.save_failed`: nothing changed; `activity.storage_failed`: the delete did not commit, the new retention may be saved

parameters.name: from

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: RFC 3339; records redeemed before it.

parameters.name: viewer

parameters.name: reward
parameters.description: Part of the reward name; ASCII letters ignore case.

400.description: `redemption.invalid_filter`: a bad time, status or page size

put.summary:
Marks a redemption of one of the toolkit's rewards fulfilled or refunds it on Twitch, then hands Twitch's answer to
the redemption records as an update, so the record changes at once (the EventSub update that follows is a
repeat).

parameters.name: twitch_id
parameters.description: Twitch's redemption ID

204.description: Done on Twitch; the record follows

403.description: `twitch.scope_required` or `rewards.not_ours` (Twitch lets only the app that made a reward handle its redemptions)

404.description: `redemptions.not_pending`: not found, or already fulfilled or refunded

502.description: `twitch.request_refused` (e.g. a channel without channel points), `twitch.rate_limited` or `twitch.unreachable`

400.description: `rewards.invalid` (no title or cost, or over Twitch's limits), `rewards.refused`, or not signed in
`rewards.invalid` (nothing to change, or over Twitch's limits), `rewards.refused`, or not signed in

403.description: `twitch.scope_required` (no `channel:manage:redemptions`) or `rewards.not_ours` (made in the Twitch dashboard or by another app)

post.summary:
Makes a toolkit reward with the original's settings under a new title, then points check-in, the reward sound
and the reward video or GIF at it. The original is left as it is: the toolkit cannot change it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The reward made in the Twitch dashboard

400.description: `rewards.invalid` (a bad title, or the reward is already the toolkit's), `rewards.refused`, or not signed in

409.description: `rewards.duplicate_title` (still the original's, or another reward's) or `rewards.limit`

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The original file name: its extension must match the content; the rest becomes the label.

Stops what 「在 OBS 播放」 sent: the test sound playing on `/overlay/sound/` and the waiting ones

Renames a sound or changes its volume.

put.summary: Records how long a sound plays; the admin window measures each sound after import, and older ones once.

400.description: `stream_info.invalid` (over Twitch's limits, checked here) or `stream_info.refused` (Twitch refused the content)

200.description: Up to 20 categories matching the query

get.summary:
The latest stream's follows, subs and resubs (each gifted sub included), cheers, raids and redemptions, one row
each, as its stats count them; `null` before the first stream. Simulated events are never stored, so never
here.
The latest stream session and what happened during it; `null` before the first stream.
The tab bar; `null` when never edited (every group pinned, on top).

put.summary:
Saves the tab bar: up to 20 group IDs of 1-32 characters `[a-z0-9-]`, duplicates keep their first position;
`null` restores the defaults.
Switches the alert overlay template and saves the choice; overlays reload it at once (`template.changed`).
Switches the chat overlay template and saves the choice; overlays reload it at once (`template.changed`).

get.summary: The text size in percent; `null` when never changed (100).

put.summary: Saves the text size: 90-150 in steps of 10.

requestBody.description: Absent: sign in with the base and the saved feature scopes.

500.description: `twitch.storage_failed`: signed out, but the stored token could not be deleted, so the next start would sign in again

put.summary: Turns the new-version check on or off; turning it on checks at once.
"Not this one": hides the notice until a newer release than `version` comes out.

get.summary: The stored avatars of these viewers, by Twitch user ID; viewers without one (yet) are left out.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Twitch user IDs, comma-separated (at most 200).

name.description: The name for a new browser source (1-100 characters); `name 2` and so on when it is taken.

overlay.description: The overlay's path and query, e.g. `/overlay/chat/`.

AfterNumbers.description:
How the admin UI's 下播後 home shows its numbers, so a streamer can look back without number anxiety. `revealed`:
numbers shown one by one while masked (the admin UI's IDs, kept until shown all or hidden again).

AlertEvent.description:
An `alert` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: the event envelope around its payload. Not kept in
snapshots, so a reloaded overlay never replays one.

AlertPayload.description: The `payload` of an `alert` event. Fields the kind does not have are left out.

durationMs.description: How long the overlay shows it; the next alert comes after this and a short pause.

message.description: Raw viewer text of a `resubscribe` or `cheer`, when there is one.

sound.description: Played once as the alert starts; chosen per kind in the sound settings.

userId.description: The viewer, or for a raid the raiding channel; `null` for an anonymous gift or cheer.

userLogin.description: `null` for an anonymous gift or cheer.

userName.description: Raw viewer text; `null` for an anonymous gift or cheer. Overlays escape it when rendering.

AlertReceivedEvent.description:
An `alert.received` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: an alert arrived, sent at once whether or not an
overlay will play it (the admin window lists it). Not kept in snapshots.

oneOf.description: `volume`: 0–100, the master volume.

AlertSound.description: The sound an alert plays: the overlay's built-in one, none, or a library sound.

AlertTemplate.description: Which built-in template the alert overlay shows.

Align.description: Which point of an item its position is: a corner, the middle of an edge, or the center.

Allowed.description:
Who may use a chat command. Each level also lets in the ones above it (subscriber, then VIP, then moderator),
and the broadcaster may always use every command.

AppearanceEvent.description:
A `screen.appearance` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it after any change and at start; the snapshot keeps
only the latest one.

AppearancePayload.description: The built-in overlays' theme and text size; also the body of `PUT /api/admin/screen-tools/appearance`.

textSize.description: Percent of each overlay's own text size: 50–200 in steps of 10.

AuthStatus.description: What the admin UI may see; never contains tokens.

BackupSizes.description: How large the data and the media in this folder are now, in bytes.

BadgeImage.description: One Twitch chat badge version and its image.

title.description: Twitch's name for it, e.g. `Moderator` (raw text).

BgmPlayerEvent.description: A `bgm.player` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; the snapshot keeps only the latest one.

BgmPlayerPayload.description:
The `payload` of a `bgm.player` event. The track is at `positionMs` at the event's `occurredAt`, and goes on
from there only while `state` is `playing` and `onAir` is true.

onAir.description: A music overlay is open in OBS; without one nothing plays and the position stands still.

playlist.description: The playlist chosen last; kept after a stop.

oneOf.description: `null` while stopped.

BgmTestEvent.description: A `bgm.test` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; never kept in snapshots.

BgmTestPayload.description:
The `payload` of a `bgm.test` event: the music overlay plays `track` from its start at `volume` for `durationMs`,
on its own and not as the player, and stops early when the player starts playing.

BoardEntry.description: One viewer on a board. `name` is viewer text: render it as text.

Bounds.description: How an item fills its bounding box: `none` scales its content by its size; the rest make its size the box.

BreakEvent.description:
A `screen.break` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it after any change and at start; the snapshot keeps only
the latest one.

BreakPayload.description: The break card. `text` and `endText` are broadcaster text: render them as text.

endText.description: Shown instead of the countdown once `endsAt` has passed; the card stays until hidden.

end_text.description: At most 100 characters after trimming; may be empty.

text.description: At most 100 characters after trimming; may be empty.

Canvas.description: The canvas size in pixels (OBS: the base resolution).

name.description: The name to put in the style.

CardLook.description: How the card looks; image URLs are `/checkin/{name}`, readable without a token.

CardPack.description: An installed pack. `name` is the pack's own text: show it as text.

CardStyleBody.description:
The stamp card's look. `title` and `description` may hold `#觀眾#`, `#章數#`, `#次數#` and `#格數#`; they are
broadcaster text, shown as text.

background_image.description: A name `POST /api/admin/checkin/images` gave; `null`: the color only.

show_repeat.description: A repeat check-in on the same business day shows the card too; nothing is recorded.

stamp_image.description: A name `POST /api/admin/checkin/images` gave; `null`: a plain stamp in the color.

ChannelReward.description: A custom reward. `title` and `prompt` are raw Twitch text.

manageable.description: Made by the toolkit, so it can change the reward and its redemptions; others are read-only here.

skip_queue.description: Redemptions are marked fulfilled at once instead of waiting in the queue.

ChatBadgeName.description: A role shown by a chat badge (a founder counts as a subscriber).

ChatDisplay.description: How the admin UI shows chat (the chat log page and the docked panel); OBS overlays follow their template.

textSize.description: Percent of the admin UI's text size, 80-150 in steps of 10 (the Host checks).

ChatDock.description:
Whether the admin UI docks the chat on wide windows, how wide (CSS pixels; the Host checks the range) and on
which side of the pages.

side.description: Missing in settings saved before the choice existed: the right side.

ChatFirstEvent.description:
A `chat.first` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: the admin window marks that message 第一次聊天. Not kept
in snapshots; the message in the snapshot carries `firstChat` instead.

ChatFirstPayload.description: The `payload` of a `chat.first` event: the message already shown that is its sender's first in the channel.

truncated.description: More messages or events than one page holds happened then; these are the latest.

ChatMessageEvent.description: A `chat.message` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: the event envelope around its payload.

badges.description: The roles the sender's badges show.

bits.description: Bits cheered with this message, when there are any.

color.description: `#RRGGBB`, or `null` when the user never picked a color.

firstChat.description:
The sender's first message in the channel, when known as it is published; a later `chat.first` says so for
a message already shown.

oneOf.description: The message this one replies to.
During a shared chat, the other channel the message was sent in.

text.description: Raw viewer text; overlays escape it when rendering.

twitchBadges.description: Every badge as Twitch names it, in Twitch's order (the admin window shows their images).

ChatPeriod.description: A stretch of time the chat log can show.

firstAt.description: When its first stored message was sent; `null` when it has none.

from.description:
RFC 3339 with microseconds, as stored, so a later query keeps the same boundary; `null` before the first
stream.

to.description: RFC 3339; `null` while it is still going.

ChatRemovedEvent.description:
A `chat.removed` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: overlays and the admin window drop those messages
(the ones before it in `seq` order). The messages it names leave the snapshot, and the latest removals are kept
in it so a window that was away can drop what it still shows.

ChatRemovedPayload.description:
The `payload` of a `chat.removed` event: a moderator took down one message (`messageId`), every recent message
of one viewer (`userId`), or the whole chat (neither).

since.description: For a viewer or the whole chat: RFC 3339, the oldest message sent time it reaches (older ones stay).

userName.description: Raw viewer text; overlays escape it when rendering.

message_id.description: Twitch's ID of the message, as chat events carry it.

ChatStyle.description: How much room each chat line takes.

ChatTemplate.description: Which template the chat overlay shows. `custom` (the data folder's `templates/chat/`) has no UI entry.

ChatTextSizeEvent.description:
A `chat.text_size` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; the snapshot keeps only the latest one, so a reloaded
overlay gets the size too.

ChatTextSizePayload.description: The chat overlay sets it as the CSS variable `--chat-text-size` on its page, which the templates' sizes read.

textSize.description: In px; `null` keeps each template's own size.

CheckinChangedEvent.description:
A `checkin.changed` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: a viewer checked in. It carries only the viewer's
ID, so viewer text stays off this event; the admin UI reloads its lists. Not kept in snapshots.

CheckinDeadLetter.description:
A redemption the check-in module failed to take five times in a row. `user_name` and `reward_title` are raw
Twitch text.

CheckinDeduction.description: One deduction in the change log. `user_name` and `reason` are raw text: escape them when rendering.

CheckinHiddenEvent.description:
A `checkin.hidden` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: 隱藏畫面卡片 takes the card on screen away at once.
Not kept in snapshots.

CheckinOutbox.description: Redemptions waiting for the check-in module (while it is paused), and those it failed to take.

oldest_pending_at.description: RFC 3339: when the oldest waiting redemption happened.

CheckinSettingsBody.description: The check-in settings. `command` is stored without its `!`; a leading one is accepted and dropped.

allowed.description: Who may check in with the command; the broadcaster always may.

command.description: One word, at most 25 characters; no other feature's command may have it (ignoring case).

reset_hour.description: Local hour a new business day starts, 0–23.

reward_id.description: Twitch ID of the channel points reward that checks in; `null`: chat only.

CheckinStampedEvent.description:
A `checkin.stamped` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: a stamp card to show on `/overlay/checkin/`. The
Host sends them one at a time. Not kept in snapshots, so a reloaded overlay never replays one.

avatarUrl.description: Twitch profile image (`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/` only); `null` when unknown.

description.description: The style's description with its variables filled in (raw text: render it as text).

durationMs.description: How long to show the card.

oneOf.description: Played once as the card shows; `null`: silent (the default).

stamps.description: Stamps on the current card, out of `slots`.

title.description: The style's title with its variables filled in (raw text: render it as text).

userName.description: Raw viewer text; overlays escape it when rendering.

CheckinToday.description: Today's check-ins (the business day in force now).

CheckinViewer.description:
One viewer with the stamp card derived from the total. `user_login` and `user_name` are raw Twitch text: escape
them when rendering.

available.description: Stamps that can be spent: `total` minus what was deducted, never below 0.

last_check_in.description: Business day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) of the latest check-in; `null` when there is none.

stamps.description: Stamps on the current card, out of `card_slots`; from `total`.

total.description: Lifetime check-ins; deductions never lower it.
Viewers matching the search, across all pages.

cancelled.description: Waiting items that will not play.

CommandTakenBody.description: The admin API's answer to `commands.taken` (409): which command already has the name.

label.description: How to name that command: what the broadcaster calls it (e.g. a counter's name), or `!<name>`.

module.description: The module whose command has it.

Connections.description: What the connection checks found just now.

eventsub_subscriptions.description: Subscriptions Twitch holds for this app and account; `null` when it could not be read.

twitch_latency_ms.description: Round trip of one Helix call; `null` when signed out or it failed.

ContestEvent.description: A `twitch.contest` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it whenever the poll or the prediction changes.

ContestPayload.description: What is on: the latest poll (`None` before any or once it was archived) and the latest prediction.

CounterBody.description: A counter with its command. `name` is broadcaster text: render it as text.

allowed.description: Who may use the command; the broadcaster always may.

command.description: The chat command without its `!`; empty: none.

per_stream.description: Back to 0 when the next stream starts.

command.description:
One word of at most 25 characters, with or without its `!`; empty: no chat command. No other command may
have it (ignoring case).

delta.description: `1` or `-1`; a counter never goes below 0.

CounterTestEvent.description:
A `counter.test` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: the counter overlay shows an extra test row for a few
seconds. Not kept in snapshots.

CounterValue.description: One counter on the overlay. `name` is broadcaster text: render it as text.

CounterValuesEvent.description:
A `counter.values` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it after any change; the snapshot keeps only the
latest one.

CounterValuesPayload.description: The `payload` of a `counter.values` event: every counter, in creation order.

amount.description: 1 to 1,000,000, and at most what is available.

DiagnosticReport.description: The diagnostic report (匯出診斷報告).

ErrorBody.description:
Body of the errors admin handlers return: a stable `<area>.<reason>` code the admin UI translates.
The missing-token 401 has an empty body, and malformed JSON gets axum's plain-text rejection.

count.description: Records older than that, which a change to it would delete now.

oneOf.description:
`alert` is its kind as in the `alert` payload (`follow`, `subscribe`, ...); `amount` the months of a resub,
the subs of a gift, the bits of a cheer or the viewers of a raid.
The reward's title (raw text).
`chat`, `redemption` or `manual`; `simulation` for a card from the simulator.

FeedItem.description: One item. `viewer` is raw viewer text: render it as text.

oneOf.description:
What it set off and what became of it; `null` when this launch does not know (it happened before a restart,
or set off nothing).

simulated.description: From the simulator (shown as 測試); never in the records.

viewer.description: `null` for an anonymous gift or cheer.

FeedOutcome.description: What became of what it set off.

FeedReason.description: Why its module turned it down, when the Host knows.

media.description: The media item's title (raw text), for a video or GIF.

oneOf.description: Why it was declined, when the Host knows; `null` otherwise.

sound.description: The reward sound's name (raw text), for a sound.

FirstRun.description: The first-run setup: shown until it is finished or skipped (`Settings::setup_finished`).

Fit.description: How a picture that is not square becomes square.

GeneralSettings.description: Settings → General. The desktop app reads the same `settings.json` flag on every ✕ of the admin window.

ask_before_close.description: Show the close hint on ✕; the hint's "Don't show again" turns it off.

settings_unreadable.description:
Read only (ignored on PUT): `settings.json` exists but cannot be read or parsed. Defaults are in use and
no setting saves (`settings.save_failed`) until the file is fixed or removed.

ImportSkip.description: An entry left out. `key` is the file's own text (at most 64 characters): escape it when rendering.

ImportSummary.description: What an import adds, updates (replacing the imported baseline of known viewers) and skips.

Input.description:
An input that has sound (the ones OBS can mute), with its fader and monitoring. Volume and monitoring belong to
the input, not to a scene.

global.description: One of OBS's global audio devices (desktop audio, mic/aux in its audio settings): heard in every scene.

scenes.description:
The scenes that contain the input: as an item, inside a group, or through a nested scene. Containing it does
not mean viewers hear it (it may be muted or monitored only).

volumeDb.description: The fader in dB (0 is full; very low values mean silent).

volume_db.description: The fader in dB, -100 to 26; absent leaves it.

InputMeter.description: An input's latest audio level, from OBS's volume meters.

peakDb.description: The loudest channel's peak in dB, after the fader; -100 means silent.

enabled.description: Shows or hides the item; absent leaves it.

locked.description: Locks or unlocks the item; absent leaves it.

oneOf.description: Puts the item at this canvas position and alignment; absent leaves it. Scale, rotation and crop stay.

position.description:
Moves the item to this place in the scene, counted front to back as `obs.state` lists items (0 is the
front); absent leaves it.

oneOf.description: Scales the item to this size in canvas pixels, each side 1-100000; absent leaves it. Position stays.

Turns, flips, crops or fits the item (only the parts given; rotation -360-360°, crop 0-100000 px a side);
absent leaves it. Position and size stay.

ItemSize.description: An item's size on the canvas: its source (less what is cropped) times its scale, in canvas pixels.

ItemTransform.description: How an item is turned, flipped, cropped and fitted, besides where it sits and how large it is.

crop.description: Source pixels cut off each side before scaling.

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise around its align point, 0-360.

LeaderboardEvent.description:
A `leaderboard.update` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it when the boards change (checked every 30 s); the
snapshot keeps only the latest one.

LogEvent.description:
A follow, sub, resub, gift, cheer, raid or redemption, placed among the messages by its time. Fields the kind
does not have are left out; names and texts are raw viewer text.

userName.description: `null` for an anonymous gift or cheer.

LogLine.description: One log line. `message` stays on this page; the report never carries it.

code.description: The error code (`<area>.<reason>`) when the line has one.

add_scopes.description: Scopes a feature needs, kept for every later sign-in too; each must be in `FEATURE_SCOPES`.

date.description: A past business day to back-fill (`YYYY-MM-DD`); omitted or `null` registers today.

minutes.description: -1440 to 1440, not 0; the remaining time stays between 0 and the cap.

MarathonEvent.description:
A `counter.marathon` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it after any change and at each live status; the
snapshot keeps only the latest one.

max_hours.description: The remaining time never goes above this many hours, 1–168.

sub_minutes.description: Minutes added per sub, resub or gifted sub, 0–1440.

MarathonPayload.description:
The sub marathon timer. The remaining time is as of the event's `occurredAt` and goes on counting down from
there only while `running`.

live.description: The toolkit has seen the stream live.

paused.description: Paused by hand; a stream starting does not resume it.

running.description: Counting down: live, not paused and time left.

MarathonTestEvent.description:
A `marathon.test` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: the marathon overlay shows a fixed time for a few
seconds. Not kept in snapshots.

MediaItem.description: One media item. `title` is broadcaster text: render it as text.

duration_ms.description: How long it shows; `null` until the admin window has read a video's length.

missing.description: The file is no longer in the data folder.

MediaPlayEvent.description:
A `screen.media` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it when its turn on the presentation queue comes, or at
once for 試播 (`source=simulation`).

MediaPlayPayload.description:
The `payload` of a `screen.media` event: the alerts overlay shows `url` at `position` for `durationMs`, a video
at `volume`. Not kept in snapshots, so a reload never shows it again.

MediaPosition.description: Where the alerts overlay shows a media item.

MediaRuleBody.description: What a channel points reward shows when redeemed.

duration_ms.description: 1 ms to 10 minutes; `null` keeps the length it has.

input.description: An OBS input's name; `null`: not chosen.

close.description:
With `enabled: false`: skip the module's outbox events instead of keeping them for later ("close"; the
default pauses). Enabling a closed module never delivers what was published while it was closed.

closed.description:
Disabled and skipping its outbox events ("close"); a disabled module that is not closed is paused and keeps
them for later.

Monitor.description: Whether OBS plays the input on the monitoring device, and whether it still goes to the stream.

MusicPlaylist.description: A playlist. `name` is broadcaster text: render it as text.

used_by.description: The names of the scene rules that play it; the admin UI lists them before deleting it.

NotEnoughStamps.description: More than is available; nothing was deducted.

password_set.description: Whether a password is stored; the password itself is never returned.

ObsPerformance.description: OBS's numbers; absent while OBS is not connected.

bitrate_kbps.description: The stream output's bitrate over the last 60 s; `null` while not streaming.

dropped_percent.description: Frames dropped (rendering and the stream output) in the last 60 s, in percent; `null` before two readings.

password.description: Absent keeps the stored password; empty removes it (OBS with authentication off).

connected.description: Whether OBS is connected; the rest is empty while it is not.

local.description:
Whether OBS runs on this computer; overlays can be added to scenes only then, since the Host's addresses
open nowhere else.

sources.description: The browser sources that show one of this Host's overlays; other browser sources are left out.

ObsStateEvent.description: An `obs.state` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; the snapshot keeps only the latest one.

ObsStatusEvent.description: An `obs.status` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; the snapshot keeps only the latest one.

ObsStatusPayload.description: The `payload` of an `obs.status` event, and the `status` of `GET /api/admin/obs`.

reason.description: Stable code such as `obs.auth_failed`; `null` when connected or right after startup.

Outcome.description: What finally became of an item, as far as the Host can tell (overlays do not report back).

OverlayCounts.description: Open overlay sockets per kind; `other` counts sockets without a known kind, the admin window included.

overlay.description: The overlay it shows: its path and query, e.g. `/overlay/leaderboard/?board=bits&period=stream`.

scenes.description: The scenes it is an item of (items inside a group are not counted).

OverlayTheme.description: A theme for the built-in overlays; custom templates never use it.

chat_missed_writes.description: Storage operations refused since launch after the bounded chat queue filled.

chat_write_delayed.description: Present while a chat record or moderation update is waiting for storage to recover.

eventsub_connected.description: The EventSub session is connected and subscribed (chat, alerts, redemptions arrive).

irc_connected.description:
Twitch's first-chat mark can be read (anonymous IRC joined); otherwise 第一次聊天 is the toolkit's first
sighting of the viewer.

scopes.description: The scopes the current sign-in granted; empty while signed out. Features check theirs against it.

PackRefused.description: Why a zip was refused; `detail` names the file (and the line and column in `index.html`).

service.description: The service whose switch turned it off.

warning.description: Dropped frames above 5 % in the last 60 s.

Placement.description: Where an item sits on the canvas: the canvas pixel its `align` point is at.

PlayResult.description: How it ended: an [`Outcome`], or `file_missing` for media whose file was gone.

PlaySound.description: A library sound to play: `url` is its file (`/sounds/{id}`), `volume` 0–100 (%).

oneOf.description: Starts `playlist` (or the last chosen one) from its start, or resumes it when it is paused.
Within the first 3 seconds the track before; later the same track from its start.
Moves within the track playing; past its end, the next one starts.

PlayerControl.description: What to do with the player.

shuffle.description: Random order instead of the playlist's own.

PlayerTrack.description: The track playing. `title` is broadcaster text: render it as text.

oneOf.description: What went wrong that the Host can see; `null` when nothing did.

PollChoiceView.description: A choice and its votes so far (channel points votes included). `title` is raw Twitch text.

PollTemplate.description: A poll saved to start again: its question, choices and how long voting lasts.

endsAt.description: RFC 3339: when voting ends, or ended.

PredictionEnd.description: What happens to a prediction: no more predictions, a winner (Twitch pays out), or canceled (Twitch refunds).

PredictionOutcomeView.description: An outcome with the viewers and channel points on it so far. `title` is raw Twitch text.

endedAt.description:
RFC 3339: when it was resolved or canceled; empty while it runs (or when Twitch did not say). The overlay
shows a result only shortly after this, so one read from an earlier stream never comes back on screen.

locksAt.description: RFC 3339: when predicting closes, or closed; empty when Twitch did not say.

PresentationQueueEvent.description: A `presentation.queue` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; the snapshot keeps only the latest one.

PresentationSkippedEvent.description:
A `presentation.skipped` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: the overlay of `stage` stops its picture and
sound at once. Not kept in snapshots.

PresentationStoppedEvent.description:
A `presentation.stopped` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: every overlay stops its picture and sound at
once. Not kept in snapshots.

Problem.description: Something the Host itself can see went wrong with an item (overlays do not report back).

deleted.description: Records deleted because the new retention no longer keeps them.

QueueStatus.description: What the queue holds right now.

oneOf.description: The item on its overlay now; `null` while nothing plays.

gapMs.description: The pause after each item, in ms.

waiting.description: In the order they will play.

RecentAlertBody.description: One alert in 最近事件.

oneOf.description: What became of it; `null` while it waits or plays.

payload.description: As the overlay gets it now (the sound follows the current settings).

RecordKind.description: One row of the stream's record: what the stats count, one row each.

RecordRetention.description: Keep records for this many days (1–3650), or forever; older ones are deleted on their own.

RecordRow.description: One row; names, messages, reward titles and inputs are raw viewer text.

gifted.description: A sub handed out by a gift.

input.description: What the viewer typed for the reward; `null` when nothing.

tier.description: 1, 2 or 3, for a sub or resub.

viewer.description: `null` for an anonymous sub or cheer.

RedemptionChangedEvent.description:
A `redemption.changed` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: a record was created or changed status. It
carries only the record ID, so viewer text stays off the overlay channel; the admin UI reloads the list.
Not kept in snapshots.

RedemptionOutcome.description: What a redemption becomes: fulfilled, or refunded (Twitch gives the points back).

failed_writes.description: Redemptions that could not be stored since the app started, even after retries; they are not in the list.

total.description: Records matching the filters, across all pages.

RedemptionRecord.description:
One redemption record. `user_name`, `reward_title` and `user_input` are raw viewer or Twitch text: escape them
when rendering.

played.description:
What the redemption played, in the order each ended: empty when it played nothing, `null` for a record
from before this was kept.

twitch_id.description: Twitch's redemption ID, for marking it fulfilled or refunding it.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC: when the record was created or last changed status.

user_input.description: Empty when the reward asks for nothing.

ReportLine.description: A log line in the report: no message text, so no names, IDs or secrets.

RestorePreview.description: What a backup holds, shown before the broadcaster confirms a restore.

app_version.description: The version of the app that made it.

contents.description: The kinds it holds: a restore replaces only these.

created_at.description: When the backup was made (RFC 3339, UTC).

Reward.description: A channel points reward of the signed-in channel, for picking the check-in reward. `title` is raw Twitch text.

RewardChange.description:
A reward's settings; fields left out stay as they are (when editing) or take Twitch's defaults (when adding,
which needs `title` and `cost`).

title.description: Up to 45 characters; unique in the channel (Twitch ignores case).

RewardUse.description: A setting that used the original reward.

items.description:
The scene's own items, front to back (as the program's source list shows them); items inside a group are
not listed.

children.description:
A group's items, front to back; empty for anything else. Commands on them take the group's name (`source`)
as the scene, and their `id`s are unique within the group.

kind.description:
What the source is: the program's input kind (OBS: `browser_source`, `game_capture`…), `scene` for a nested
scene, `group` for a group; empty when the program does not say.

locked.description: Whether the item is locked against moving it by mistake in the program.

SceneRuleBody.description: A playlist that plays on some OBS scenes. `name` and `scenes` are broadcaster text: render them as text.

autoplay.description: Switching to one of its scenes starts its playlist.

id.description: Empty for a new rule; the Host gives it one.

playlist.description: `null` once its playlist was deleted; an enabled rule needs one.

scenes.description: OBS scene names, compared without regard to case; at most 256 characters each.

stop_on_leave.description: Switching away to a scene whose rule does not autoplay stops the music.

ScriptRefused.description: Why a script was refused: the line when the JSON itself is broken, or the step that does not fit.

line.description: 1-based line in the file of broken JSON.

step.description: 1-based number of a step that is not a known kind or misses a field.

duration_ms.description: When the last step plays, at the chosen speed.

ServiceUse.description:
Twitch or OBS not used at all (設定 › 功能): `unused` lists them; `parked` are the modules that were on and were
turned off because of it, so turning the service back on turns exactly those on again.

SharedChannelPayload.description: Another channel in a shared chat.

ShowBreakBody.description: Shows the card: give `minutes` (1–1440) or `until` (UTC, RFC 3339, within the next 24 hours).

amount.description:
Months (`resubscribe`), subs (`gift`, 1 to 100), Bits (`cheer`) or raiders (`raid`), 1 to 100000;
ignored for the other kinds.

message.description: Up to 500 characters (`resubscribe`, `cheer`); ignored for the other kinds.

stamps.description: Stamps on the card, 1 to its slots; all of them shows the full-card effect.

too_large.description: A badge still above 25 KB after reducing its colors.

stage.description: The overlay whose item was skipped.

sound.description: A sound's ID, `silent`, or `null` for the slot's default.

Snapshot.description: The first message on `/ws/overlay`: the recent retained events of each type.

bgm.player.description: At most one: the latest background music player status.

chat.removed.description: The latest removals, oldest first: what was taken down before this snapshot.

chat.text_size.description: At most one: the chat overlay's text size.

counter.marathon.description: At most one: the latest sub marathon timer.

counter.values.description: At most one: every counter's latest value.

leaderboard.update.description: At most one: the latest leaderboard.

obs.state.description: At most one: the latest streaming-software state.

obs.status.description: At most one: the latest status.

presentation.queue.description: At most one: the latest presentation queue status.

screen.appearance.description: At most one: the built-in overlays' theme and text size.

screen.break.description: At most one: the break card.

screen.warnings.description: At most one: the on-stream warnings.

stream.status.description: At most one: the latest live state.

twitch.contest.description: At most one: the latest poll.

Sound.description: One imported sound. `label` is broadcaster text: render it as text. Its file is `GET /sounds/{id}`.

duration_ms.description: How long it plays; `null` until the admin window has measured it (`PUT /api/admin/sounds/{id}/duration`).

used_by.description: Slots that play it; deleting it puts them back to their defaults.

duration_ms.description: How long the sound plays, 1 ms to 6 hours.

slots.description:
Chosen slots: `alert.<kind>`, `checkin`, `checkin.full` or `reward.<Twitch reward ID>` → a sound's ID or
`silent`. A slot left out plays its default: the built-in sound for alerts, nothing otherwise.

volume.description: Master volume, 0–100 (%), applied on top of each sound's own.

SoundPlayEvent.description:
A `sound.play` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: a reward sound for `/overlay/sound/`, which plays them
one at a time in order. Not kept in snapshots, so nothing replays after a reload or restart.

SoundStoppedEvent.description:
A `sound.stopped` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it: `/overlay/sound/` silences the test sound playing
(`sound.play` with `source=simulation`) and drops the waiting ones; reward sounds play on. Not kept in snapshots.

SoundStoppedPayload.description: Empty: the event itself is the stop.

Source.description: Where an event came from. Simulated events never go into real business records.

fields.description: Fields of the source's form to change; the rest of its settings stay.

SourceFamily.description: The kinds of source with a form; any other (a plugin's included) is shown as "change it in OBS".

value.description: What the field is set to for this choice.

fields.description: Only the fields of this kind's form; a browser source's `url` only when it opens this Host's overlay.

url_hidden.description: A browser source opening another address: it is not shown, and can be changed in OBS only.

Stage.description: The overlay that presents an item.

cancelled.description: Waiting items that will not play.

deleted.description: A moderator took it down; its text and fragments are empty.

id.description: Twitch's message ID, the same as the live `chat.message` event's `id`.

oneOf.description: `None`: no category set.

language.description: ISO 639-1, e.g. `zh`; `other` when Twitch has none for it.

StreamRecord.description: The latest stream session and what its stats count, row by row, to export.

StreamStatusEvent.description: A `stream.status` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; the snapshot keeps only the latest one.

viewers.description: While live, once a check has counted them (every minute).

chatMessages.description: Chat messages from Twitch stored for the session.

endedAt.description: `null` while live (or until the end is seen).

endedSinceLaunch.description: The stream ended while this Host was running.

firstChats.description: Viewers' first messages in the channel (第一次聊天) during the session.

peakViewers.description: The most viewers a check counted; `null` until one has.

subs.description: New subs and resubs, each gifted sub included.

StreamingState.description: What the streaming software shows right now; [`StreamingState::default`] while it is not connected.

preview.description: The scene in the preview while studio mode is on; `null` otherwise.

scene.description: The scene on air; `null` while not connected (unknown).

studioMode.description:
Whether the program's studio mode is on: picking a scene puts it in the preview, and a transition puts the
preview on air.

transitions.description: The transitions to pick from, in the program's order.

oneOf.description:
An alert; `alert` is its kind as in the `alert` payload (`follow`, `subscribe`, ...). No viewer for an
anonymous gift or cheer.
A stamp card with `stamps` of its `slots` filled.
A reward sound and the viewer who redeemed it.
A reward's video or GIF and the viewer who redeemed it.

Subject.description: What an item is, as the queue area names it; names are raw text.

TabBar.description:
Which tab groups the admin UI pins in its tab bar, in order (the rest go into "More"; `[]` pins none), and
where the bar sits. The Host checks the format only; which group IDs exist is the admin UI's business.

moved.description: Settings now pointing at the new reward.

not_moved.description: Settings that still point at the original: saving them failed, so the broadcaster picks the new reward there.

pause_failed.description: The original is paused, but pausing the new reward failed: viewers can redeem it until it is paused here.

title.description: The new reward's title; Twitch refuses the original's while that one exists.

TemplateChangedEvent.description: A `template.changed` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it; not kept in snapshots.

error.description:
With `custom` selected: `template.missing`, `template.unreadable` or `template.invalid` while overlays
get the default template instead of the user's; otherwise `null`.

TestOverlay.description: Which overlay gets a test value.

Track.description: One imported track. `title` is broadcaster text: render it as text. Its file is `GET /music/{id}`.

duration_ms.description: How long it plays; `null` until the admin window has measured it (`PUT /api/admin/music/{id}/duration`).

missing.description: Its file is gone from the music folder (deleted outside the app).

used_by.description: The names of the scene rules whose playlist has it; the admin UI lists them before deleting it.

duration_ms.description: How long the track plays, 1 ms to 24 hours.

playlists.description: Every playlist the track should be in; it joins the end of new ones and leaves the others.

TransformChange.description: A transform change: only the parts given change; the rest of the item's transform stays.

transition.description: One of `obs.state`'s `transitions`; absent keeps the one in use.

TwitchBadgePayload.description: A chat badge as Twitch names it.

id.description: The version within the set (e.g. a subscriber badge's tier and months).

info.description: Extra info, e.g. the months subscribed; often empty.

available.description: The newer release to tell the broadcaster about; `null`: no notice.

check.description: Whether the new-version check is on (Settings → General).

size.description: The backup file's size in bytes.

ViewerCountBody.description: One viewer's count. `login` and `display_name` are viewer text: render them as text.

ViewerCounterBody.description: A count kept per viewer. `name` is broadcaster text: render it as text.

top.description: The three viewers with the most, most first.

delta.description: `1` or `-1`; a count never goes below 0.

twitch_user_id.description: A viewer from the viewer directory.

onAir.description: Its overlay is open in OBS right now; when it is not as its turn comes, the item is skipped.

mic_input.description: An OBS audio input name; `null` or blank: the mic is not checked.

WarningsEvent.description:
A `screen.warnings` event exactly as `/ws/overlay` sends it after any change and at start; the snapshot keeps
only the latest one.

WarningsPayload.description:
Which warnings are on and what was last seen. The overlay shows a warning that is on and down; the mic one only
once `micMutedSince` is `micSeconds` old.

chatOverlayDown.description: No chat overlay is open in OBS.

micInput.description: The OBS audio input watched; `null`: the mic is not checked.

micMissing.description: The watched input is no longer in OBS: pick another.

micMutedSince.description: UTC, RFC 3339: since when the watched input has been muted.

twitchDown.description: The Twitch event connection is down.
